sources.title: Miss Annabelle Lee — Polydor 21768

sources.researchNote: The upload title gives 1927 without distinguishing the composition, recording or issue. The earlier editorial date [1928] was inferred from nearby catalogue numbers, not from a dated entry for Polydor 21768 itself; it is not retained as an established issue date. The label and transfer identify the two-piano partnership, but an exact session or issue date remains unverified.

sources.shortCitation: Polydor 10237-B, “Song is ended” — Hermann Bick and Dr. Kaper
sources.fullCitation: Hermann Bick and Dr. Kaper (two pianos). “Song is ended” / “唄ひ終わりて.” Boston; music credited to Berlin. Polydor 10237-B, label matrix 1774 BK, manufactured in Japan by Nippon Polydor Chikuonki Co., Ltd., Tokio, n.d. Label reproduced in the YouTube transfer published by 梅園 真澄, 25 June 2026.
sources.title: 唄ひ終わりて (Song is ended) — Hermann Bick & Dr. Kaper, Polydor 10237-B
sources.creator: Hermann Bick and Dr. Kaper
sources.researchNote: The readable label directly identifies the two pianists, title, Berlin credit, catalogue number 10237-B, matrix 1774 BK and Japanese manufacturer. It does not supply a session or issue date. 25 June 2026 dates the YouTube access copy, not the historical disc. M231 remains a documentary still of the label, not an audio asset.

sources.fullCitation: Ilja Livschakoff Tanzorchester. “Ein Lied aus meiner Heimat.” Slowfox from Melodie der Liebe. YouTube transfer; the uploader identifies Polydor 24604, matrix 4735 BD VII, and reports a Berlin recording session around May 1932.
sources.title: Ein Lied aus meiner Heimat — Polydor 24604
sources.creator: Ilja Livschakoff Tanzorchester
sources.researchNote: The catalogue number, matrix, performer and film identification are supplied by the uploader; they have not been independently corroborated for this transfer. The description explicitly says “Aufnahme: Berlin, ca. Mai 1932”, so the source date describes an approximate reported recording session, not an issue date. Other recordings of the song, including the Rosvaenge/Livschakoff master 4733 ½ BD, are not evidence for matrix 4735 BD VII.

works.title: Le bistrot du port
works.publicNote: Valse written for the singer Lys Gauty, to words by Gaston Groener and A. Saudemont; the printed edition (Paris: Coda, cop. 1934) credits the music to Pierre Candel, a pseudonym standing here for Kaper and Jurmann together. In his 1975 AFI oral history Kaper recalled it as the last song he wrote in Paris, and said he never heard it there before leaving for the United States.
